subject: RAG fit follow-up: retriever choices, reranker tradeoffs, and QA benchmarks
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@orpheus-analytics.com>, Alex Cho <alex.cho@orpheus-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RAG fit follow-up: retriever choices, reranker tradeoffs, and QA benchmarks

Hi Maya / Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal (from your side): deliver an internal Q&A assistant that returns grounded passages from Orpheus docs with high precision@1 and a low hallucination rate for compliance summaries.
- Key constraints: ~300ms 95p per-query latency target for the UI, single-region (us-west) deployment, and retention policy that keeps embeddings for 18 months.

Attached is a short evaluation plan (20270914-orpheus-rag-eval-plan.xlsx) and our initial prompt set (prompt-set-v1.jsonl). High-level recommendations from the call:

1) Retriever: start with a sparse+dense hybrid. We suggest BM25 for recall + a small dense ANN index (multi-vector where possible) using OpenEmbed-3-small embeddings for phrase-level recall.
2) Reranker: run a lightweight cross-encoder (distil-cross-enc-bert-small) in the rerank stage to optimize precision@1; use the larger cross-encoder only for long-tail heavy queries.
3) Grounding metrics to track: precision@1, recall@5, attribution-F1 (span-level), and hallucination-rate (rate at which answers include unsupported facts).

Ask: can you confirm the three canonical doc sources (Product Spec, Regulatory Pack, Support KB)? If yes, we’ll run an initial 500-query benchmark next week against those and share the dashboard.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Today: you confirm doc sources + share Drive folder link.
- Wed (09/16): Redwood runs automated retrieval + reranker baseline and shares benchmark link (approx 500 queries).
- Fri (09/17): Quick sync to review results and decide on reranker sizing and caching policy.

If you want, Ben can include a short appendix on quantization choices for the reranker (uint8 vs q4_k) and the expected latency delta.

Thanks —
Logan

--
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@orpheus-analytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@orpheus-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RAG fit follow-up: retriever choices, reranker tradeoffs, and QA benchmarks

Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the three doc sources: Product Spec, Regulatory Pack, Support KB (all in the folder I shared with Alex). We’ll add a short readme so you can map canonical IDs.

A couple of quick clarifications:
- For latency, the 300ms 95p is a UI commitment; we can tolerate some background calls up to 700ms for longer reranks.
- We currently have about ~1.2M docs (mixed sizes) and expect a monthly growth of ~5–7%.

I’m curious about the hybrid approach — do you recommend combining BM25 + dense embeddings at query time or running BM25 as a recall pass then ANN on top? Also appreciate the quantization appendix; Alex will want numbers for cost estimates.

We’re good with the proposed timeline. Looking forward to the initial benchmark.

Best,
Maya

--
Maya Patel
Product Owner, Orpheus Analytics
maya.patel@orpheus-analytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@orpheus-analytics.com>, Alex Cho <alex.cho@orpheus-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RAG fit follow-up: retriever choices, reranker tradeoffs, and QA benchmarks

Logan / team —

Adding some concrete technical recs for the evaluation run tomorrow:

1) Retriever config (baseline run)
- Sparse: BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75) against full text index.
- Dense: OpenEmbed-3-small embeddings (384d), ANN using HNSW with ef_search=128, M=32. Index stored in single-shard per 300k docs.
- Hybrid: recall = union(top-200 BM25, top-200 ANN) then dedupe by passage id.

2) Chunking strategy
- Chunk size: 400 tokens with 50 token overlap for long specs. For short KB articles, keep whole doc.

3) Reranker options
- Fast path: distil-cross-enc-bert-small (quantize to q4_k on GPU for latency) — expected rerank latency per-query ~120–180ms depending on top-K (K=20).
- High-accuracy path: cross-enc-bert-large for batched offline scoring during low-traffic windows (used for model validation / nightly re-rank).

4) Monitoring thresholds to detect quality regression
- Precision@1 must stay >= 0.82 on the sample evaluation set.
- Attribution-F1 >= 0.78.
- Hallucination rate <= 6% (measured on curated ground-truth prompts).

5) Prompting notes (from initial prompt set)
- Use a two-stage template: (A) retrieval-augmented context + (B) answer-generation with explicit "cite:" requirement (force structured citations).
- Save all prompt+context pairs for drift monitoring.

Attachments: small appendix with expected latency/cost for quantization options (BenQ-quant-appendix.pdf stub referenced in spreadsheet).

If Maya’s team agrees with the hybrid recall union and the K=20 rerank cutoff, we’ll run the baseline with those settings tomorrow morning.

-Ben

--
Ben Carter
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RAG fit follow-up: retriever choices, reranker tradeoffs, and QA benchmarks

Hi Maya / Alex —

Thanks for confirming the folders. Operational items from our side: 

- We’ll spin up a dedicated experiment run in us-west with the configs Ben listed. Expect a dashboard link in ~24 hours.
- Data handling / retention: our default embedding TTL is 18 months; we’ll surface a retention policy doc for you to sign off.
- SLA implications: using the cross-encoder on the fast path (even quantized) will increase your reserved compute needs; we’ll include cost delta in the benchmark report.

Action items for Orpheus:
- Share drive folder with read permissions for redwood-eval@redwoodinference.com by EOD.
- Confirm acceptance of the hybrid recall union and K=20 rerank cutoff.

Monitoring / alerting we’ll set up for the pilot:
- Daily pipeline health (indexing lag, embedding failures).
- Weekly precision@1 and hallucination-rate reports with rolling 7-day windows.
- Alert: precision@1 drop > 5 percentage points in a 48-hour window triggers a canary rollback to previous reranker weights.

We’ll also save the prompt-set-v1.jsonl examples in the experiment results so you can replay them for regression tests.

Thanks —
Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions PM, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: RAG fit follow-up: retriever choices, reranker tradeoffs, and QA benchmarks

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful. We’ve shared the Drive folder (link in a separate share). Confirming: hybrid recall union + K=20 rerank cutoff accepted.

We’ve also invited redwood-eval@redwoodinference.com to the folder. Please run the initial 500-query baseline and send the dashboard link when ready.

One final ask from procurement: Alex (CC) will need the quantization cost appendix and an estimate of monthly reserved GPU hours if we keep the fast cross-encoder path at 95p latency targeting 300ms. If you can include a short table in the benchmark report, that would help speed approvals.

Appreciate the clear plan — speak after you publish results.

-Alex
